podcast.body: Benefiting from the coattails of "Let's Dance," this album shot to number 1 in the UK, reached the top 10 in the US, and became Bowie's second ever platinum LP in America. Despite its commercial success, critics were nearly universal in their scorn for the album, and Bowie himself later apologized for its quality. "Blue Jean was the lead single of Tonight, David Bowie's 1984 album, benefiting from the co-tails of Let's Dance."

podcast.body: This album, a rushed follow-up to "Let's Dance," was intended to capitalize on Bowie's newfound mainstream audience but was largely unsuccessful. Reviews for the record and its accompanying tours were generally unkind. "Maybe the less said about the Tonight album and that never let me down album the better."

podcast.body: This album, featuring the song "Blue Jean," was a rushed follow-up to "Let's Dance," intended to capitalize on his new audience but failed to connect. Critics widely dismissed it as merely "Let's Dance Part 2," noting a stark absence of the innovation typically expected from Bowie. "The big knock against that record was that it wasn't anything more than Let's Dance Part 2."
